scenes.headline: How LoT spends tokens only where the detail goes
scenes.sub: A diffusion transformer that is told in advance where detail matters.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tessera! Image models spend the same compute on a blank wall as on a face. This model is told where the detail goes.

scenes.text: Tile the token grid with rectangles: fine tokens where a layout asks for detail, coarse tokens everywhere else.
scenes.mark: fine tokens where a layout asks for detail
scenes.say: Tile the token grid with rectangles. Small ones where a layout says detail matters, big ones elsewhere.

scenes.credit: LoT project page data, drawn by me
scenes.title: A real layout

steps.say: Here is a real layout. Plain letters at the top sit on big tokens, and the empty background gets the biggest.
The flowered letters at the bottom get the smallest tokens, and that is where the picture puts its finest detail.
Each rectangle of the noisy latent is projected down to one token, with a matrix fitted for its size.
The transformer runs on that short sequence. Each token's rotary position sits at its centre, and an embedding tells it its size.
Each token leaves through a head for its size, which predicts the whole clean patch underneath.
The noise the token never saw is recovered by algebra from the sampler's own state. So every step still updates every latent pixel.

scenes.title: Where the full velocity comes from
scenes.text: u = P u_A + (I - P)(x_t + u_A) / t

parts.note: what the token could see, predicted
parts.say: The first term lives in the subspace the token could see. The network predicts it.

parts.note: the rest, read off the noisy state
parts.say: The second term is computed from the noisy state. No network involved.

scenes.title: Speedup from the paper's tables
scenes.say: Speed depends on sequence length. An image with nearly three times fewer tokens runs twice as fast. A long video with that cut runs three and a half times faster.

scenes.label: of the subject lands in the fine-token box, against 45.38% dense
scenes.say: The layout also steers the picture. Move the fine tokens, and the subject tends to follow.

scenes.text: The layout is a plan, and the plan sets the compute. Long sequences gain more than the token cut.
scenes.say: The layout is a plan, and the plan sets the compute. Longer sequences gain the most.

recap: Tile the token grid by detail
Project, denoise, recover the full velocity
scenes.say: Tile by detail. Project, denoise, recover. And expect video to gain the most.
